In summary, our research is concerned with
the physical mechanisms that trigger the activity in the nuclei of galaxies and the evolution of QSOs, ULIGs, starbursts and their host galaxies.
the physical conditions under which QSOs are produced.
the origin and early evolution of QSOs and the role of mergers and interactions in their formation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

QSOs, ULIGs, mergers, and starburst activity are all intimately related, and that the transition QSOs studied in this paper provide strong observational support for the merger hypothesis of QSO formation.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

ULIGs and QSOs are two manifestations of the same phenomenon: a major merger of gas-rich disk galaxies, which leads to the formation of a compact, massive, starbursting nucleus, which in turn powers a QSO and/or ULIG phase.
the transition QSOs in this study are young, massive galaxies in the process of forming stars at a high rate.
ULIGs and QSOs share a common evolutionary path and are the result of mergers.

QSOs, at least in this sample, are young systems.
the QSO phenomenon is closely related to strong tidal interactions or major mergers.
